subject: anatomy
title: Digestive system and gland histology: key high-yield facts

steps.tx: The **oesophagus** wall has four layers: mucosa, submucosa, muscularis externa and adventitia. The mucosa is lined by **stratified squamous non-keratinised** epithelium, and the serosa is absent except over a short lower segment. The muscularis externa is striated in the upper third, mixed in the middle third and smooth in the lower third.
steps.say: The oesophagus wall has four layers: mucosa, submucosa, muscularis externa and adventitia. The mucosa is lined by stratified squamous non-keratinised epithelium. A serosa is absent except over a short lower segment. The muscularis externa is striated in the upper third, mixed in the middle third and smooth in the lower third.

steps.tx: The **gastric glands** of the body and fundus contain parietal cells, chief cells and mucous neck cells. **Parietal cells** secrete hydrochloric acid and intrinsic factor, and sit in the middle and basal parts of the gland. **Chief cells** secrete pepsinogen and lie near the base. Goblet cells are normally absent from the stomach.

steps.tx: **Brunner glands** are compound tubuloalveolar glands in the submucosa of the duodenum, mainly between the pylorus and the papilla of Vater. They secrete alkaline mucus that neutralises acidic chyme. They also release urogastrone, which is human epidermal growth factor and inhibits acid production. They are absent from the jejunum, ileum and colon.

vis.alt: Layered diagram of the duodenal wall from the lumen outward: mucosa with villi and crypts, muscularis mucosae, submucosa containing Brunner glands that secrete alkaline mucus, muscularis externa and outer adventitia or serosa.
vis.caption: Brunner glands in the submucosa are the histological signature of the duodenum.

steps.tx: **Paneth cells** sit at the base of the crypts of Lieberkuhn in the small intestine. They are rich in zinc, rough endoplasmic reticulum and eosinophilic granules containing lysozyme and defensins. Unlike most epithelial cells, they do not migrate up the villi and stay near the crypt base. **Goblet cells** secrete mucin and are found in the small intestine, colon, trachea and conjunctiva.

steps.tx: The **liver lobule** is the classic unit centred on a central vein, with a portal triad at each corner. A **portal triad** holds a hepatic artery branch, a portal vein branch and a bile duct. The **space of Disse** lies between hepatocytes and sinusoids, and hepatocyte microvilli project into it. **Kupffer cells** are fixed macrophages lining the sinusoids, mainly in the liver.

steps.tx: Serous acini secrete watery fluid and have round, dark nuclei, whereas **mucous acini** are larger, have flattened nuclei pushed to the base and stain pale with haematoxylin and eosin. **Myoepithelial (basket) cells** lie between secretory cells and the basal lamina and squeeze secretions out. The **myenteric plexus of Auerbach** lies between the muscle layers along the whole gut.

vis.caption: Serous cells: round nuclei, dark. Mucous cells: flattened basal nuclei, pale.
